title: What does XLS-40 specify for DIDs?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-40 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-40 specifies decentralized identifiers anchored to XRPL account-controlled ledger entries. [1]

The ledger can carry or reference DID-related information, and the account controls updates or deletion according to the protocol. Identity resolution is distinct from due diligence: a self-controlled identifier does not independently establish a legal name, qualification or licensing status. Consumers still need to decide what evidence and external documents they trust for the intended purpose. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-40 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-40 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
